author: Francesco Mattana
title: Ragù di Funghi - Mushroom Ragu
ingredients: Grana Padano or Pecorino to serve (optional)
instructions_list: Clean and roughly chop the mushrooms. Finely chop the rosemary and sage, then place the mushrooms in a large roasting tray. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil and season with salt, pepper, rosemary and sage. Use your hands to toss everything together, making sure the mushrooms are evenly coated.
Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until the mushrooms are deeply golden and have released most of their moisture. Roasting them first intensifies their flavour and gives the ragù a much richer taste.

Meanwhile, finely dice the onion, carrot and celery to make the soffritto. Heat a generous drizzle of olive oil in a large casserole or saucepan over a medium heat. Add the vegetables, season with a generous pinch of salt and cook gently for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft.
Add the tomato paste and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring continuously.

Once the mushrooms are roasted, add them to the soffritto, together with the bay leaves. Stir well, then pour in the white wine. Allow it to bubble for a couple of minutes so the alcohol can evaporate.
Pour in the vegetable stock, reduce the heat to low and leave the ragù to simmer gently for 20 minutes, allowing all the flavours to come together.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the mascarpone until you have a rich and creamy mushroom ragù. Stir through the freshly chopped parsley, then cover and set aside.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of generously salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta until al dente, following the cooking time on the packet.
Bring the mushroom ragù back to a medium heat. Drain the pasta, reserving some of the cooking water, and add the pasta directly to the sauce.
Toss everything together over the heat, adding a little pasta water at a time until the sauce becomes glossy and coats the pasta beautifully.
Turn off the heat, add the grated Grana Padano or Pecorino and toss well. Adjust the consistency with a final splash of pasta water if needed. Serve immediately.
description: This is the perfect autumn pasta recipe. It's inspired by a northern Italian Ragù di Funghi as you’ll find lots of wild mushrooms there at this time of year. It's perfect with pasta, on top of polenta or even as a lasagna filling! I like to finish it with mascarpone for a creamy sauce, but you can also use tomato passata for a delicious vegan version. *For a red and vegan version: replace the mascarpone with 400g tomato passata and use a vegetarian/vegan hard cheese, or leave out the cheese altogether
